cs.t:
Let me tell you about last week then and why I quit. Google Fi couldn't activate my new unlocked Motorola phone that I bought from Amazon, using a SIM card they mailed me. They blamed the SIM card and had me order another, which got lost in the mail because they used a courier called TForce (look them up, look at the reviews, they're a network of volunteers using their cars). In the end I had ordered 11 SIM cards and 3 new phones from Amazon, one of them being the very shitty Motorola G Power 2021 that I'm cursed to have to type this on right now. Until my iPhone 13 arrives. Google support were totally clueless and my support agent didn't even know I had moved to TMobile. In the nearly 2 weeks without service I lost tens of thousands of dollars and I may sue. Also I discovered I was paying $50 for unlimited voice and 2GB of data, but TMobile sold me a plan that delivers that for $15! Seriously, and they're running from the same network. Android has a different philosophy to QA than iOS. Google is very happy to ship defective software relying on OTA updates later to resolve the issues. With a Pixel phone you're a beta tester. I had 8+ crashes when setting up the Pixel 5 and 4A devices. And the hardware was flakey AF. 
If you think those products are worth paying for it's because you have no point of reference. Seriously, literally, Google should pay YOU to beta test their crap.
